# Server TypeScript migration (Phase 3)

Goal: convert every first-party .js file under server/ and index.js to TypeScript, one batch (directory) at a time. The vendored code in server/libs and all files under test/ stay as they are.

## Rules (apply to every batch)
1. At the end of every batch `npm run build:server` must report 0 "error TS" and `npm test` must show 356 passing, 0 failing. Never end a session with a red build.
2. Do not edit, skip or delete any test. Do not change files outside the batch unless a type error in the batch cannot be fixed otherwise; list any such change in the Log below.
3. Runtime behaviour must not change. Do not fix bugs. When types expose a bug, keep the behaviour, add a `NOTE:` comment at that line and add one line to the Bugs section below.
4. No `any`, no `@ts-ignore`, no `@ts-nocheck`, no `@ts-expect-error`. Use `unknown` and narrow it. Every type assertion (`as`) needs a one-line comment.
5. Module style (copied from Phase 1 and 2): local modules use `import X = require('./X')` and `export = X`, so existing require() callers, tests and sinon stubs keep working. Third-party packages with a default export use `import x from 'pkg'`.
6. Shared types live next to the data they describe (see server/providers/types.ts). Add a types.ts in the directory when two or more files share a type.
7. Convert with `git mv X.js X.ts` so history is kept. Keep JSDoc descriptions and drop JSDoc type annotations that the signature now carries.
8. At the end of each batch: update the Progress table, commit with the message `phase3 batch N: <directory>`, and stop.

## Progress
| Batch | Directory | Files | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | server/utils (all subfolders) | 46 | done |
| 2 | server/objects (all subfolders) | 18 | done |
| 3 | server/models | 25 | 3a done, 3b done, 3c done (QueryFindOptions replaced by RuntimeFindOptions) |
| 4 | server/auth and server/routers | 6 | done |
| 5 | server/managers | 18 | done |
| 6 | server/scanner | 13 | done |
| 7 | server/controllers (remaining 22) | 22 | done: 20 converted, 2 skipped (LibraryController, LibraryItemController; see Skipped files) |
| 8 | server/migrations | 15 | todo |
| 9 | server top-level files (Logger, Database, Auth, SocketAuthority, Watcher, Server) and index.js | 7 | todo |
| 10 | Packaging: package.json scripts, Dockerfile and anything else that references a .js entry point | 0 | todo |

Already done in Phase 2: server/finders, server/providers, server/controllers/SearchController.

## Bugs found (not fixed)
Each has a `NOTE:` comment at the line.
- server/utils/generators/opmlGenerator.ts: reads `podcast.itunesPageUrl` but the Podcast model field is `itunesPageURL`, so the OPML outline never gets an `htmlUrl`.
- server/utils/podcastUtils.ts `extractImage`: xml2js puts `<image>` in an array, so `channel.image.url` is always undefined and the RSS `<image><url>` is never used (always falls back to `itunes:image`).
- server/utils/podcastUtils.ts `extractEpisodeData`: the second `media:content` find does not require a url, so an audio `media:content` without a url makes `enclosure.url.trim()` throw.
- server/utils/scandir.ts `groupFileItemsIntoLibraryItemDirs`: a media file in the folder root is stored as a string group; if a directory has the same name, `.push` is called on that string and throws (2 places).
- server/utils/parsers/parseFullName.ts: `fixCase !== 'undefined'` compares with the string 'undefined' instead of using typeof, so that part of the check is always true.
- server/utils/parsers/parseFullName.ts `fixParsedNameCase`: the suffix check indexes `namePartLabels[j]` (word index) instead of `namePartLabels[i]` (label index).
- server/utils/comicBookExtractors.ts `CbzComicBookExtractor.open`: `getBuffer()` can return null, which is passed to `Archive.open` unchecked (the class is not used by `createComicBookExtractor` at the moment).
- server/utils/migrations/dbMigration.ts `handleOldLibraries`: maps `oldDbIdMap.libraries[library.oldLibraryId]`, but the Library model has no `oldLibraryId` (it was just written to `extraData`), so the key is "undefined" and old library ids in users' `librariesAccessible` are mapped to undefined and dropped.
- server/objects/files/LibraryFile.ts `setDataFromPath`: `getFileTimestampsWithIno` returns `false` when stat fails; the file is then created with `ino` undefined and no size/timestamps, and no error is reported.
- server/auth/TokenManager.ts `rotateTokensForSession`: when the conditional update hits 0 rows and the session row has been deleted in the meantime, `findOne` returns null and `updatedSession.refreshToken` throws.
- server/auth/OidcAuthStrategy.ts `verifyCallback`: when no user matches and auto-register is off, `user.isActive` is read on null and throws a TypeError, so the intended 'User not active or not found' error is never thrown (the login still fails, the log shows the TypeError).
- server/routers/ApiRouter.ts `getUserListeningStatsHelpers`: reads `s.lastUpdate`, but PlaybackSession has no `lastUpdate` (it is `updatedAt`), so `items[id].lastUpdate` is always undefined.
- server/models/Collection.ts `getOldCollectionsJsonExpanded`: the permission-filtered books are assigned to `this.books`, which in this static method is the Collection class, not the collection `c`; `c.toOldJSONExpanded()` then uses the unfiltered `c.books`, so users with tag or explicit-content restrictions get every book of a collection they can see (and the class gets a stray `books` property).
- server/models/Library.ts `getMaxDisplayOrder`: `this.max('displayOrder') || 0` applies `|| 0` to the promise, which is always truthy, so with no libraries it resolves to null instead of 0.
- server/models/Author.ts `getAllLibraryItemsForAuthor`: `author.books` is read without checking that `findByPk` found the author, so an unknown author id throws a TypeError.
- server/models/Feed.ts `updateFeedForEntity`: when the library item, collection or series of the feed no longer exists, `getExpandedById` returns null and `getFeedObjFor...` throws a TypeError before the try block (3 places), so the caller gets an exception instead of null.
- server/models/Playlist.ts `checkHasMediaItem`: without an episodeId it reads `pmi.mediaItem.libraryItem.id` for every item, but a podcast episode media item has no `libraryItem` (it is on `episode.podcast`), so it throws a TypeError for playlists that contain episodes.
- server/models/PodcastEpisode.ts `createFromRssPodcastEpisode`: RSS chapters can have `end: null` (the RSS parser types them so), and they are stored in the `chapters` column, which everything else reads as chapters with a numeric end.
- server/models/LibraryItem.ts `saveMetadataFile`: the podcast branch writes `asin: mediaExpanded.asin`, but Podcast has no asin, so it is always undefined (and left out of metadata.json).
- server/models/User.ts `checkCanAccessLibraryItem`: `libraryItem.media.metadata?.explicit` reads a property of the old models; Book and Podcast have no `metadata`, so that half of the explicit check is always false.
- server/models/Session.ts `refreshToken` (with server/auth/TokenManager.ts `createTokensAndSession`, `rotateTokensForSession`): the column is NOT NULL, but TokenManager writes `generateRefreshToken` results, which are null when signing fails; the create/update then fails validation and throws instead of reporting the signing error.
- server/managers/NotificationManager.ts `onTest`: calls `triggerNotification('onTest')` without event data; `getApprisePayload` then reads the template variables from undefined and throws a TypeError for the default onTest templates (`{{version}}`). onTest is not called anywhere at the moment.
- server/managers/CronManager.ts `checkUpdatePodcastCron`: the log title falls back to `libraryItem.media.metadata?.title`, an old-model property; Podcast has no `metadata`, so the fallback is always undefined.
- server/managers/RssFeedManager.ts `checkFeedRequiresUpdate`: when the library item, collection or series of a feed no longer exists, `getEntity` returns null and the next read throws a TypeError (2 places); `getFeed`: when `updateFeedForEntity` returns null, `feed.buildXml` throws a TypeError.
- server/managers/PodcastManager.ts `createPodcastsFromFeedUrls`: when `getFileTimestampsWithIno` fails (returns false), the library item is created with `ino` undefined and the timestamps 0; when the feed title is empty or not a string, `sanitizeFilename` returns false, so the podcast path ends in "/false" and `relPath` is false.
- server/managers/CoverSearchManager.ts `startSearch`: on a failed search it calls `onError(error.message)`, but onError takes (provider, errorMessage), so the client gets the message as the provider and an undefined error.
- server/managers/MigrationManager.ts constructor: the default `configPath = global.configPath` reads a global that is never set (the global is `ConfigPath`); Database passes the path, so the default is not used.
- server/scanner/MediaProbeData.ts `setData`: prober accepts a file with only a video stream; `audio_stream` is then null and the reads of `this.audioStream` throw a TypeError, which prober.probe returns as the error (so the AudioFileScanner "no audio stream" message is not used for such files).
- server/scanner/AudioFileScanner.ts `getTrackAndDiscNumberFromFilename`: reads `author` and `series` from the filename metadata, which has `authors` and `seriesName`, so the author and series are never removed from the filename; `partbasename.replace(publishedYear)` has no replacement, so the year is replaced with the string "undefined".
- server/scanner/PodcastScanner.ts `saveMetadataFile`: writes `asin: libraryItem.media.asin`, but Podcast has no asin, so it is always undefined (same as LibraryItem `saveMetadataFile`).
- server/scanner/LibraryItemScanner.ts `getLibraryItemScanData`: when `getFileTimestampsWithIno` fails (returns false), the scan data gets `ino` undefined and the timestamps 0.
- server/scanner/Scanner.ts `quickMatchLibraryItem`: `PodcastFinder.search` returns null for a podcast without a title, and `results.length` then throws a TypeError.
- server/scanner/LibraryScanner.ts `scanLibrary`: when a library item is removed while the scan runs, `getExpandedById` returns null and the null is pushed to the updated items and emitted to clients (`items_updated`).
- server/controllers/SessionController.ts `getTrack`: `getUserById` returns null when the user was deleted while the session is open; the debug log then reads `user.username` and throws a TypeError (the async handler rejects, no response is sent).
- server/controllers/PlaylistController.ts `addBatch`: the `episodeId` of an item is not checked against the podcast's episodes (and the item may be a book); for an unknown episode `episode.toOldJSONExpanded` throws a TypeError (for a book `podcastEpisodes.find` throws), after nothing was saved.
- server/controllers/UserController.ts `update`: `user.permissions.itemTagsSelected.join` / `librariesAccessible.join` throw a TypeError if the stored permissions lack these keys (UserPermissions allows that for older users; the User model reads them with `|| []`).
- server/controllers/UserController.ts `delete`: the playback sessions of the deleted user get `userId: null`, while the PlaybackSession model types `userId` as string.
- server/controllers/AuthorController.ts `update`: `name: null` passes the payload check, so the author name is saved as null (the column allows it), while Author.name is typed string.
- server/controllers/ApiKeyController.ts `create`: `permissions` is not set, so the column is null, while the ApiKey model types it as required (nothing reads it at the moment).
- server/controllers/ShareController.ts `createMediaItemShare`: `pash` is not set (null) and `expiresAt` can be null, while the MediaItemShare model types them as string and Date.
- server/controllers/PodcastController.ts `create`: when `getFileTimestampsWithIno` fails (returns false), the library item is created with `ino` undefined and the timestamps 0 (same as PodcastManager `createPodcastsFromFeedUrls`).

## Log
### Batch 1: server/utils (46 files, all converted, none skipped)
- New type files: `server/utils/types.ts` (shared utils types, `declare global` for the `global.*` values used in utils, and typed views of untyped vendored libs/models), `server/utils/parsers/types.ts`, `server/utils/queries/types.ts`, and `server/utils/ssrf-req-filter.d.ts` (ssrf-req-filter has no types; tsconfig excludes `*.d.ts`, so it is pulled in with a `/// <reference>` from `server/utils/types.ts`).
- devDependencies added (rule 10): `@types/express`, `@types/xml2js`, `@types/uuid`. They were already in node_modules as extraneous packages; `npm install` also pruned the other extraneous ones locally (`@types/passport`, `@types/cookie-parser`, `@types/express-session`, `@types/passport-strategy` ...), so later batches must add those to devDependencies when they need them.
- No files outside server/utils were changed (apart from package.json/package-lock.json and this file). No tests were changed.
- Module style: every module now ends in `export = <object/class/function>`. Modules that used `module.exports.x = ...` export one object literal with the same keys; checked that no utils module is in a require cycle, so assembling the export object at the end is safe. Internal `this.x()` / `module.exports.x()` calls go through that object, so sinon stubs on exports keep working. Compared `Object.keys`/`typeof` of every compiled module against HEAD: identical, except `parseFullName` is now a `function` declaration (needed for overloads) instead of an arrow function, so it has a `prototype`.
- Typed views for untyped JS (each a single commented `as` where the module is required): `FsExtra` for libs/fsExtra (its fs API is built at runtime), `ArchiverFactory` for libs/archiver, `SortInstance` for libs/fastSort, the fuse.js constructor in podcastUtils, ffprobe in prober, libarchive in comicBookExtractors.
- `TypedDatabase` (utils/types.ts): the JS models override `Model.init` with a different signature, so TypeScript rejects their static query methods (`findAll`, `count`, ...). Files that query cast `require('../../Database')` to `TypedDatabase` (same object; model getters still read lazily). It also types `sequelize` as set and `libraryFilterData`. Batch 3 (models) should make this unnecessary.
- Model associations (`book.libraryItem`, `series.bookSeries`, `mediaProgress.mediaItem`, ...) and JSON columns (`user.permissions`, `user.extraData`, `playbackSession.mediaMetadata`) are not declared on the JS models; the queries describe the loaded rows locally and cast once per query result. Sequelize's types are stricter than what it accepts at runtime (arrays of where options, `limit: null`, `[literal]` order items, a single nested include object, `distinct` on findAll, `limit` on count); those option objects use `QueryFindOptions` or are cast at the call with a comment.
- Behaviour-neutral code changes made for typing: `new Date() - n` became `new Date().valueOf() - n` (same coercion); a few repeated reads were pulled into a commented local (`permissions`, `mediaMetadata`, `models`); `getMediaGroupQuery` in libraryItemsBookFilters writes properties through a `mediaWhereHash` alias of the same object; `libraryFilters.getFilterData` replaces its sets with arrays through a typed alias of the same object; zipHelpers no longer requires express at runtime (it was only used for a JSDoc type); dbMigration no longer destructures the unused `QueryInterface` value from sequelize.
- JSDoc in not yet converted JS files that points at typedefs which moved (`import('../utils/fileUtils').FilePathItem`, `import('../utils/podcastUtils').RssPodcast*`, `import('./parseEbookMetadata').EBookFileScanData`) now resolves to `any` in those JS files; point them at `server/utils/types.ts`, `podcastUtils.ts` or `parsers/types.ts` when those files are converted.
- Incremental tsc crash: changing `server/utils/types.ts` (its `declare global` block) makes `tsc` crash with `Debug Failure. False expression` in `getSpecifierForModuleSymbol` while re-emitting signatures of JS files. A clean build works; fix with `rm dist-server/.tsbuildinfo`.
- Result: `npm run build:server` reports 0 `error TS`; `npm test` 356 passing, 0 failing.

### Batch 1 fixes (after independent review)
- abmetadataGenerator: restored the original `validated.series?.length` truthiness check (the batch had changed it to `Array.isArray(...) && ...length`); `series` is now typed `unknown[]` instead of using an `as`.
- Class fields declared without an initialiser in comicBookExtractors, utils/index (ValidationError, NotFoundError), rateLimiterFactory and longTimeout compiled to `field;` lines that created own properties set to undefined. They are now `declare` fields (rule 12) and compile to nothing, as in the JavaScript.
- Tried `"useDefineForClassFields": false` in tsconfig.server.json first and reverted it: it changed the compiled output of 21 files, including about 10 JS files that are not converted yet (ApiCacheManager, Database, Logger, TokenManager, MigrationManager, BinaryManager, User, DeviceInfo, ServerSettings, BookScanner), where real field initialisers move into the constructor body after parameter defaults. ApiCacheManager's `new LRUCache(this.defaultCacheOptions)` default then reads undefined and throws (348 passing, 1 failing).

### Batch 2 and 4: server/objects, server/auth, server/routers (24 files, all converted, none skipped)
- New type files: `server/objects/types.ts` (`FileMetadataJSON`, `AudioChapter`, `TaskString`, and `DateAndTime`, a typed view of the minified vendored libs/dateAndTime used by objects and ApiRouter) and `server/auth/types.ts` (`declare global`: `Express.User` extends the User model so `req.user` is typed, and `var RouterBasePath`; `PassportDone`, `JwtPayload`).
- devDependencies added (rule 10): `@types/passport` (passport.use/unuse and `req.user`), `@types/express-session` (`req.session` in OidcAuthStrategy).
- No files outside the batch were changed (apart from package.json/package-lock.json and this file). No tests were changed.
- Class fields: every field the JS assigned in the constructor or later (none were JS class fields) is a `declare` field (rule 12), so the classes compile to the same constructor bodies. The JS static field initialisers (`DeviceInfo.stringFields`, `ServerSettings.patchableSettingsKeys`, `TokenManager.TokenSecret`) stay normal static fields. `Task.failedAt` and `TrackProgressMonitor.currentTrackProgress`, set outside the constructor, are declared too.
- Fields the JS JSDoc typed as non-null but initialised to null (`AudioFile.metadata`/`metaTags`, `LibraryFile.metadata`, `EBookFile.metadata`, `PodcastEpisodeDownload.rssPodcastEpisode`/`libraryItem`/`url`) keep the non-null type with a commented `null as unknown as T` in the constructor; other null-initialised fields are typed `T | null`.

import re,glob
for f in sorted(glob.glob('v*.ts')):
    s=open(f).read()
    n0=len(s)
    # 1. remove typedef block
    s,c1=re.subn(r'/\*\*\n \* @typedef MigrationContext\n(?: \*.*\n)*? \*/\n\n', '', s, count=1)
    # 2. module style
    s=s.replace("const util = require('util')", "import util = require('util')")
    s=s.replace("const { Sequelize } = require('sequelize')\n", "import sequelize = require('sequelize')\n")
    # add type import after the last top import, or at top
    imp="import type { MigrationOptions } from './types'\n"
    m=list(re.finditer(r'^import .*\n', s, re.M))
    if m:
        e=m[-1].end(); s=s[:e]+imp+s[e:]
    else:
        s=imp+'\n'+s
    # 3. signatures
    s,c3=re.subn(r'async function (up|down)\(\{ context: \{ queryInterface, logger \} \}\)', r'async function \1({ context: { queryInterface, logger } }: MigrationOptions): Promise<void>', s)
    # 4. jsdoc
    s=s.replace('@param {MigrationOptions} options', '@param options')
    s=s.replace('@returns {Promise<void>} - A promise', '@returns A promise')
    # 5. export
    s,c5=re.subn(r'^module\.exports = \{ up, down \}$', 'export = { up, down }', s, flags=re.M)
    open(f,'w').write(s)
    print(f, c1, c3, c5)
EOF

143	 * @param {ConstraintUpdateObj[]} constraints
144	 * @returns {Promise<Record<string, SequelizeFKObj>|null>}

146	async function getUpdatedForeignKeys(queryInterface, tableName, constraints) {
147	  const execQuery = queryInterface.sequelize.query.bind(queryInterface.sequelize)
148	  const quotedTableName = queryInterface.quoteIdentifier(tableName)
149	
150	  const foreignKeys = await execQuery(`PRAGMA foreign_key_list(${quotedTableName});`)
151	
152	  let hasUpdates = false
153	  const foreignKeysByColName = foreignKeys.reduce((prev, curr) => {
154	    const fk = formatFKsPragmaToSequelizeFK(curr)
155	
156	    const constraint = constraints.find((c) => c.field === curr.from)
157	    if (constraint && (constraint.onDelete !== fk.onDelete || constraint.onUpdate !== fk.onUpdate)) {
158	      fk.onDelete = constraint.onDelete
159	      fk.onUpdate = constraint.onUpdate
160	      hasUpdates = true
161	    }
162	
163	    return { ...prev, [curr.from]: fk }
164	  }, {})

EOF

Batch 8 is committed as `phase3 batch 8: server/migrations` (dd0b7b2f) and the working tree is clean. All 15 migrations are converted and none were skipped.

**File count:** 15 `.js` files, the same as the Progress table. The folder also has `changelog.md` and `readme.md`, which aren't code. HEAD was batch 7 and the tree was clean before I started.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Build:** a clean `npm run build:server` reports 0 `error TS`.
- **Tests:** `npm test` shows 356 passing and 0 failing. No test was edited, skipped or deleted.
- **Behaviour:** no condition, SQL string or expression was rewritten. Every compiled file outside server/migrations is byte-identical to the pre-batch build. Of the 15 compiled migrations, 12 are identical; the other 3 differ only by `require` lines (listed in the Log).
- **Files outside server/migrations:** only MIGRATION.md changed.

**How the files are found (what I checked)**
- At runtime MigrationManager copies every `.js` file from `dist-server/server/migrations` into `<config>/migrations`.
- It then throws for any `.js` file there whose name has no version.
- It loads each file with `Module._compile` and reads `up`/`down`. The applied migrations are stored by file name, including `.js`.
- The tests require `server/migrations/<name>` from the compiled output.
- So the compiled names stay `<name>.js`, the exports stay `{ up, down }`, and the stored names are unchanged.

**Where the context type went:** a `types.ts` in server/migrations would compile to `types.js`. MigrationManager would copy it and reject it, and every start with an existing database would fail. So the context type is in `server/migrations/types.d.ts`, which emits no JS. MigrationManager has no named context type to reuse; it types the context as `unknown`. The build skips type-checking `.d.ts` files, so I checked it separately and confirmed its types resolve rather than silently becoming `any`.

**Casts (rule 17)**
- **Totals:** 32 `as`, 1 `as unknown as`, 1 `!`.
- **By tag:** b 27, d 6 (none tagged a or c).
- **Exception 1 (catch variables):** 6 in total, 2 each in v2.17.7, v2.19.1 and v2.20.0. No other exception was needed.
- **Largest target types:** three types have 6 casts each, so none is over 10.
- **Shared cause:** 13 casts across 4 different target types all exist because Sequelize's types leave out `Sequelize.DataTypes`, the data types and `QueryTypes`, which are set on the class at runtime. That's under the limit by your definition of a kind, but it's one missing shared type. I noted it for batch 11 and didn't add a new shared type.

**Code changes beyond annotations (in the Log)**
- v2.19.4 never uses `util`, so TypeScript would have dropped its `require('util')`. I kept it as `import 'util'`, the same pattern batch 7 used.
- v2.20.0 now gets `Sequelize` through `import sequelize = require('sequelize')`, matching the module style of earlier batches.

**Bug (listed, not fixed):** `v2.17.0 down` changes `mediaItemShares` without the `tableExists` check that `up` has. A downgrade of a database without that table would throw. There's a NOTE at the line and an entry under Bugs.

**Server run with an empty config**
- **Fresh database:** the log says "Database is new. Skipping migrations." Exactly the 15 compiled migrations were copied to `config/migrations`.
  - /status, /init, /login and GET /api/libraries, /api/me, /api/users all returned 200, and a wrong password returned 401.
  - The only error in the log was that wrong-password attempt.
- **All 15 migrations run:** I set the database version back to 2.14.0 and restarted. All 15 ran in order through the real loader, the database ended at 2.37.0, and the same requests returned the same codes.
  - v2.17.3 logged a caught SQLite trigger error and rolled back that one step. That's because it ran against a 2.37.0 schema that already has later triggers.
  - The pre-batch JS build produces an identical log in the same setup, so the error isn't from the conversion.

One slip: a comparison command passed `/dev/null` to my test script, which deletes its target folder first. The delete failed because I'm not root, and I confirmed /dev/null is intact.

I've stopped here; batch 9 hasn't been started.
